utterances.text: We suggest that we make a break here. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination. Mr. Scott. Cross-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I think hopefully I just have a few questions for you. Perhaps if we can clarify a few things or confirm a few things at the beginning, the rest of it may go fairly quickly. Did I understand you to say, sir, that you performed electrical repair work on electronic equipment and that sort of thing for Stela while he was at that time in the HOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, you continued to provide those kinds of services to Stela during 1993, during the, if you will, the Muslim/Croat conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes, and for other battalions, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was my next question. Did you do that sort of work also for the -- for the man you identified in your testimony as Baja? Did you do electronic repair work for Baja's unit as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about this man, formally known as Mario Milicevic, also known as Baja, how did you know him before you saw him on the 10th of May, 1993? What was your history, if you will, with Baja?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct, then, to say that in addition to the prior relationship or friendship you had with the Martinovic family, you also had at least to some extent a similar prior friendship with the Milicevic family. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did I understand you correctly to say, sir, that it was when you saw Baja on the 10th of May that it was sometime about an hour and a half after that that you then came into contact with Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that it's your conclusion, or the inference that you would draw, is the reason that Stela came to you was because you had first run into Baja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that with any certainty, but I believe it was he who told him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The paper that Stela and Baja, between the two of them, gave you that said you were a member of the HVO, the paper that you said they gave you for purposes of protection, that document was not true, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It wasn't. It was forged, simply to sell me as a cover. It has not been put on record anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge, sir, that similar false or forged documents were provided to other Muslims or other persons by Stela during 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: He gave papers to everybody for flats. He covered many Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so far as you know, were these statements -- are these papers again to the effect that these persons, perhaps the men in these families, were member of the HVO when, in fact, they were not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Those were papers which said that the flat concerned is under his control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how would it be the case, sir, if you can assist the Judges, how would a flat, in a particular part of Mostar, be under Stela's control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: On my flat, it said that the flat is under the control of Benko Penavic ATG, and my paper, the paper that I carried around, says that I'm a member of the Benko Penavic ATG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I appreciate that, sir. But can you give us some additional insight, beyond that, to how it would be that a sign on your door - and I'm just looking to use your words as much as possible- that "the flat is under the control of Benko Penavic ATG"? How would it be that that statement on your door would give you protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Any paper, either from the HVO or the military police or any unit in the town of Mostar, was respected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the second of the two events that you told the Judges about, in terms of times when Stela personally intervened in some way in connection with you or perhaps on some other occasion, the time that -- with the situation where a woman was evicted, you said, did I hear you say that that was approximately three or four months after the conflict in Mostar began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the conflict began in about the 9th or 10th of May, 1993, is it your best recollection that that particular event happened sometime in approximately August or September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I cannot be quite precise because those were funny times, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would agree that your prior testimony and you're sticking with your testimony as it were, sir, that it was some three or four months after the events of about the 9th and 10th of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Well, I would say so. I cannot really affirm that, but I believe somebody's already mentioned it so that perhaps the exact date is known, because dates are not my strong point really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I also confirm, sir, if I heard your testimony correctly, and I wasn't sure if you perhaps modified it at some point, that's why I'm asking you, is it your testimony, sir, that you were never yourself at the confrontation line in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I wasn't, no. I was never at the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we understand, sir, that whatever other assistance you may be able to give to the Court, whatever other assistance you can give, you simply have no information about anything that happened at the confrontation line, no firsthand information? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to touch back again briefly on the 9th and 10th of May. On the 9th of May you stayed in your flat with your family. And again, if I heard you well, you did not venture out that day at all. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your flat, could you see anything happening in Mostar on the 9th of May, or is it your testimony that you just simply saw nothing that was happening that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: From my flat, you cannot see what goes on. And all we could know was that we heard the gunfire and - I don't know - shells. I don't know. I mean, one could hear gunfire, but you can't see anything from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a similar question, sir, about the first part of July 1993, which perhaps you will recall was another date in which there was a high level of armed activity of sorts. Where were you at about the early part of July when these events happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I do not remember. Could you be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, well, perhaps you will recall that there were at least in the period from May to the end of June, beginning of July 1993, two large events in which a number of Muslims in Mostar were arrested or rounded up, if you will, perhaps other times in between. But those two particular dates seem to be a matter of, I think, common knowledge among those of us in the courtroom, and perhaps others. Do you remember a second major wave of arrest of Muslims in Mostar about the 1st of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few questions, sir, about your coming here as a witness. I heard you say, and I want to know that I did hear you say, and I want you to understand that you said when you heard about the indictment you decided on your own you wanted to come and be a witness for Mr. Martinovic. I understand that. But how did you express your willingness to come as a witness? Who did you contact to actually make the arrangements, get on the witness list, so to speak, and make the arrangements to come to The Hague? Who did you contact for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: His brother said if there is anything I can do, then I'll go and testify. About a month or perhaps two later, his lawyers came, they called me, and I communicated with them and I offered that if necessary, I was ready to go to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stela's brother come to you or contact you by telephone or come to your flat or did you initiate contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I was the one who asked for a contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just tell us very briefly, how is it that you made that contact then. Just describe to us. Did you pick up a telephone? Did you see him in the street? How was it that you had contact with Mr. Martinovic's brother about being a witness in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: His office is not far from where I am, and I was sitting in the coffee bar and I saw some people I knew come in. I asked them what it's about, and they said we're going to testify. And then I approached him sitting quite near him. I said, "Then, why not me? Why didn't you call me?" So I offered to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, sir, that you consider yourself to be good friends with Mr. Martinovic, that is, Stela, and you consider yourself to be good friends with him still today? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, can you confirm, in fact, that when you came in to the courtroom a few minutes ago, an hour or so ago, in fact you exchanged looks and smiles with Mr. Martinovic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness to be shown the map that Defence counsel used with the witness, so I can use the same -- with counsel's permission, I would use the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we go to the private session, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether you knew Mr. Takac or not, did you ever hear of an incident where someone, whether it was Mr. Takac or someone else, associated with Mr. Martinovic's unit, Stela's unit, assisted a former JNA officer in crossing the confrontation line and then having him cross back over again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm now going to page 4, item numbered 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, ever, sir, that members of various ATG units in Mostar were hiding many Muslims in the town and giving them protection in exchange for financial gain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm now referring to page 2 of Exhibit P588, toward the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any discussion or have any information come to your attention, sir, during Mostar during this time, that is, the summer and fall of 1993, that both the Mrmak and the Benko Penavic ATGs were frequently transferring civilians around Mostar and across the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally in this regard, on Exhibit P664.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever hear of a situation of a woman named Delilovic who was taken by Stela to the Croatian border and released there in exchange for money? Or perhaps, let me correct that, exchange may have a different -- released, she was released for which she or members of her family had paid money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it's correct, isn't it, that during the time when you were at Stela's headquarters, again, at one point you said virtually every day, there were never any members of the Red Cross or members of any other international organisations that came to the headquarters, were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, there were, is that there were international -- excuse me, representatives of international organisations who came to the headquarters? I'm not sure I understand your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: You asked me if there were any Red Cross people, and I said yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately when you recall these Red Cross people coming to Stela's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It was after the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So sometime after 1995, then, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes, or it could have been 1994, late that year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it's correct, isn't it, that during the times that you were at Stela's headquarters in 1993, throughout that time period no international organisation, no member of the Red Cross, no member of something that you might know as the ECMM or the European Monitoring Mission, no such individuals ever came to Stela's headquarters? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: From what I could see, they would move down the street. But I didn't see them park their vehicle and communicate with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, sir, that Mr. Martinovic would not allow any international organisations in his area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Well, they drove up and down in front of the base nonstop. As about the rest, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time period again, sir, are you talking about? When you said "They were driving up and down in front of the base" what time period were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: It was at the time when one could write by the Red Cross those messages. One could send them. And that was in 1994, I think the latter half when it became possible to write to one's kin, to one's people, when everybody could write.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that even as late as approximately June 1994, Stela was keeping skilled prisoners at his headquarters, or about that area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we are entering an area that falls outside the indictment and that should be disallowed for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's outside the indictment. Mr. Scott, you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is it correct, sir, that these prisoners, some of these -- approximately these seven to ten prisoners that we've discussed earlier, continued to work at or about Stela's headquarters in a work shop or in a garage or around that area at least until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object again because the term "prisoners" is being used, and we do not know whether they were prisoners at the time. I believe that the term should be "those people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, let us use this term, "that seven to ten people." We know who these people are, no matter we call them prisoners or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those individuals, sir, that we've talked about, and you know I believe which ones, the seven to ten individuals that you've identified earlier, the skilled labourers, the skilled workers, did they continue to be at Stela's headquarters at least until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I cannot tell you a precise date, but when an agreement was reached that prisoners were to be released, he released them. And they volunteered to work in Smajo Zikic's garage. They worked there and were paid for their services. They didn't want to go anywhere else. They stayed there to work. Those from Mostar went home to sleep at nights, the others remained there. They were free to leave if they wanted to; they just wanted to stay. I cannot talk about dates, but I know that when it was said they should be released, they were released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the problem is, sir, you just said you can't indicate dates. So you don't know if that was sometime in the second half of 1994 or 1995. You don't know when that was. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date, but in relation to the Dayton Accord, and the signatures when the army and the HVO signed that agreement that they should be released, that was when they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from the Judges? Judge Clark. Questions by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I don't have many questions, but I just would like Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. some clarification on a number of issues. When you were eventually given a uniform, Mr. Witness, did it have any markings on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just a plain camouflage uniform, not even with HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes. It was a camouflage HVO uniform. Everybody had the same sort of uniform. It was the same sort of uniform worn by HVO soldiers. They were all the same, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. If I recollect your evidence correctly, I believe you said that you worked during the conflict with the Serbs providing a service to Mr. Vinko Martinovic as an electrician and to other units as well. Where was Mr. Martinovic's headquarters during the Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: The headquarters was across the road from the old hospital in Mostar. That's the former military barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Across from the hospital, is that near the hospital that's near the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: The Ero Hotel where the Bulevar is, when you go towards the avenue, it's halfway towards it. So one might say it was near.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The Ero Hotel we've heard mentioned before. I think it subsequently became the HVO headquarters, or certainly it played a role during the war. Can I take it that the headquarters, then, was a totally different place to the headquarters during the war after the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You told us that you were subjected to a number of eviction attempts. And on one occasion after the 9th of May, it's not the 10th of May, after I think you said it was two weeks later, a neighbour sent the child on a bicycle to inform Mr. Martinovic what was happening. It seemed to me that you were talking about the headquarters at Kalemova Street. Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So by the middle of May, if I understand you correctly, Mr. Vinko Martinovic had set up a headquarters in Kalemova Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And did I understand you correctly that on the occasion that you went there, there were a couple of -- a few prisoners there, and your information in relation to the arrest and detention of the miscreants came from the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you remember that you described to us that there were a group of people who were pretending or misrepresenting themselves to be part of Mr. Martinovic's unit? So I called them "miscreants," the people who had committed the offence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Your information came from the prisoners in mid-May. My final question will require me, or the Court, to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only this map, D2/32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand this might be used by both parties. Are we going to give you one number, or double numbers? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm fine, the Prosecution is fine with giving it one exhibit number with the Defence number as long as obviously both sides, or all sides, can refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So that map D2/32 marked by the witness is admitted into evidence. Mr. Scott, do you have any evidence to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The way that it actually went. In fact all the exhibits that were referred to that were on our list have already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And this D2/31 is under seal as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The marked map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The marked map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I have a moment of the Court's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, unless something has changed and I'm not aware of it, we only have two witnesses now to complete between now and the end of our session on Thursday. I suspect there's probably a very good chance that we will actually complete those witnesses tomorrow, I would suspect. Which I don't think is bad news to anyone perhaps. And I'm not suggesting otherwise. But the reason I wanted to have some of your time now, do I want to raise some important concerns that I think are very pressing for the purposes of planning the sessions, when we immediately return from the recess. And I raise it now because I don't want to wait even until next week, because of course, it will be up to the Chamber to decide. But I'm going to suggest to the Chamber that there may be some serious questions that need to be addressed. And I don't want to put it off until the end of the day tomorrow because there, again, human nature being what it is and all of us being perhaps anxious to do other things, that we would then not get to it at the end of the day tomorrow. So that's why I think since I don't think we'll have any trouble completing the next two witnesses this week, I was going to suggest to the Chamber that now may be a good as time as any to raise some concerns with the Chamber, if I have the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any problems with Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do have some comments, and an objection. The Defence has its tempo, witnesses waiting outside. I work quite fast, although I am not as optimistic as to assume that we will finish at a quarter to 2.00 with this witness. Tomorrow, there will be time left to raise any issues about the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, we still have two days for two witnesses, according to the speed we are now, I think we could finish the last witness for this week tomorrow afternoon or Thursday morning. If we finish that witness Thursday and we have plenty time to deal with those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, I'm in the Chamber's hands, Your Honour. I don't want the week to somehow slip by and out of any ill will by anyone. These are significant issues and I'm going to suggest to the Chamber respectfully they are going to be more than five-minute issues. I'm not suggesting that we get into it now, I'm not arguing with the Chamber at all. But I do want to put it on the Chamber's agenda, because it will have a definite impact potentially on the schedule when we return from recess, in terms of some of the concerns that the Prosecution has. I will put all those other concerns off, Mr. President, as you've directed, save one short item, and that is we would like to receive, and again, because potentially tomorrow will be our last session this week, we would like to know the witnesses for next week. As I stand here before you right now, I have no idea who is coming next week, and we would like to organise ourselves. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to ask Defence counsel to furnish that list for next week by tomorrow. And we'll have time after we hear the two witnesses this week to deal with the issue that might be raised by the Prosecutor, no matter whether that will be tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. Having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Seric, we have to finish this morning's sitting at quarter to 2.00 sharply. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the Chamber has granted protective measures so that your image will be distorted, your voice will also be distorted and you will have a pseudonym. To begin with, the usher will show you a sheet of paper with your first and last name. Please don't read it out Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. loud, but simply say "yes" if it's correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will put questions to you. Please look at the light on the microphone. When I switch my microphone off, the light will go out, and only then should you begin your answer. First, I will ask you for some information about you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And so I request, Mr. President, that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us briefly what happened to you during the Serbian aggression against Mostar? How did you spend that period, and were you active in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: I stayed at home. I was not active in the military. I did my job. I walked around Balinovac, where my friends were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the 9th of May when the conflict broke out between the army of BH and the HVO in Mostar? Where were you and what happened to you on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: On that day, the 9th of May, in the morning, some soldiers came. They took me out of my house and sent me to the Velez stadium. I spent the whole day there. And in the evening, they took me to the Ero Hotel. And on the following morning, they put me in a bus and took me to the Heliodrom. I spent about nine days there, and a friend of mine whom I knew from before, got me out and took me home. He brought me home in the afternoon, and the following morning, I didn't know what to do. So I went to look for Stela to see what I would do next. And he told me, there would be no problem. He told me to go home. He asked me if I needed any money. He gave me some money. And I went home. I bought some food because there was nothing in the house. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any work in your workshop after that? It was wartime after at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Well, there was work from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone threaten you in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: On one occasion, a soldier came by car. It was a big car, and he wanted us to repair his car. He was a little drunk, and he threatened me. He said, "If his car was not ready by evening, he would kill us," me and a friend of mine. It was impossible to repair the car by the evening, and I told him it wasn't possible to repair the car in one day, that there was at least two days' work. He said: "I don't care. I'm going to a cafe to have a drink, and if it's not ready by evening, I'll kill you." I said to my friend: "I don't know what to do. I'll go to Stela's and see if he can intervene." I went to Stela's headquarters where he had meetings and I told him that a soldier had threatened to kill me if I didn't fix his car on the same day and there was no way that could be done. He told me and my friend to stay in his headquarters, and he went to look for that soldier with some of his men. After a certain time had elapsed, his soldier came to fetch my friend and me and took us back to our workshop. When we got there, we saw Stela and the soldier who had threatened me. And he said: "There's no problem. Everything is all right. Repair the car when you can." And so things after that went well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout that period, especially in late 1993 and early 1994, did anything happen in your immediate family that caused you to go to Stela for help again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Yes. In March 1994, my mother died. At that time, it was wartime, and I didn't know how to arrange for a funeral. I went to look for Stela, and I told him my mother had died. I asked him to help me bury her according to the Islamic law. He said to me: "There's no problem. Do you need anything?" He said he would give me whatever I needed. He also gave me some money. I went home and arranged for the Muslim funeral. There was a hodza who came to officiate. And everything was done at Stela's expense. At that time, it was unimaginable to have a Muslim funeral for a Bosniak family in that part of Mostar. All that ended well, and I am still grateful to Stela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any other examples where Vinko Martinovic helped somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Yes, the whole area up from, Djikovina and all the families, everybody there said how Stela had helped them, how he had brought them home from a medical school, there are quite a number of families who are grateful to Stela for what he did for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you heard of stories about Stela and Stelici, Stela's boys, persecuting Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it on various occasions. Once Stela had brought his car to me to do some repairs. It was very hot that day, and he gave me some money to go and get a beer in a shop. And the shop is quite near, not less than a one metres away from my work shop. So I went to get that beer, and there were lots of people in that shop. And I heard them talking. Stela, he's rounding people up around the market and so on and so forth. And I took those beer bottles and said: "Listen, people, Stela is at my place in the garage with his car. He gave me the money to buy beer, and I'll be off. So go out and you'll see him. He'll be passing by in 20 minutes' time" and they just stayed mum. And those are only stories, Stela does this, and Stela does that, but Stela is at a completely different place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that prisoners from the Heliodrom came to work at Vinko Martinovic's base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that. There were three or four of those prisoners. Well, they were called prisoners, but they had nothing. They worked in my garage. They walked around freely, nobody guarded them. Nothing, they had what to eat, they had what to drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pay them when they worked at your place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Well, at times somebody paid, and then we bought -- we would buy meat together and then make barbecues and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That house and that workshop, how far is it from Vinko Martinovic's base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Less than 10 minutes on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see what happened to those prisoners who were at the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can because they move about freely. Nothing. They walked around, and I know how they patronised various coffee bars and they were left alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the indictment says that it was Stela's private prison.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MH
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe it or not, Your Honours, I am done. I have finished my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's the record time in these proceedings. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But I will not finish it in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course not. Cross-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If a clean version of 11.18 could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Counsel didn't ask you to mark the map but I will because I just think it's going to be better in the long run if we have maps marked. If you can, sir, if you can look at the map that's to your right now, and orient yourself for a moment. What I'm going to ask you to do is to mark --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry. We could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. I think he needs his glasses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at the map, orient yourself for a moment, please, as best you can, and can you find on the map approximately, and it doesn't have to be terribly precise, but as close as you can where your house -- where your residence was located during 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. In private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And during your stay here in The Hague, do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony because you are still under the oath. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll resume in Courtroom I tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
